description: OFRAME, the French Organisation for Applied Research in Space Weather, coordinates research between space weather scientists and end users and runs the meteo-espace.fr site. Its data and services section offers space weather bulletins, a real-time space weather dashboard organised from the Sun through the interplanetary medium and the magnetosphere to the upper atmosphere, pages on space-based and ground-based instruments, recently funded space weather projects, and the space weather services maintained by CNRS-INSU. The current conditions panel links the Nançay radioheliograph, SOHO HMI, LASCO C2 and EIT 195 images, the Pic du Midi and Meteospace observations and the Nançay decametric array, and the site posts news such as bulletins and meetings (the European Space Weather Week 2025 and the Space Weather Days 2026 in France). Access is free online; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the dashboard gathers products from many providers, so terms and archives follow each source, and the page read gives no archive. Coverage is France, with global solar and near-Earth context. It supports space weather hazard analysis and emergency response planning for power grids, GNSS and radio communications in France; related records are BASS2000, the Met Office space weather forecast and the ESA Space Weather Service Network.
